hook.line: The year Solitaire came with Windows 3.0 — it is said to have doubled as practice for dragging with a mouse.
hook.say: Welcome to the story of the one-player card game.

ch.say: Born in Europe, it found its way to every PC.
p: Records of “patience”, cards played alone, appear in northern Europe in the late 18th century.
It became fashionable in 19th-century France and Britain. In North America it was called solitaire, and the gold-rush name “Klondike” became its most famous game.

ch.say: It’s closely tied to the history of the PC.
tl: Patience appears in a German games book
Guidebooks published in Britain spread the craze
The Klondike gold rush — later a game’s name
FreeCell is born on the PLATO education system
FreeCell and Spider join Windows too

ch.say: Red and black alternate, King on down!
ch.cap: A Klondike column: alternate colours, one rank lower each time
p: On the tableau you build down — K, Q, J… — alternating red and black.
Finish by stacking each suit from Ace to King. Half luck, half planning.

ch.say: There are hundreds of solitaire games.
cards: The most famous solitaire, with seven columns
Two decks, 104 cards: complete runs in one suit
Four free cells — almost every deal can be solved
Tradition says he played patience in exile, and some games bear his name (the truth is unknown)
Windows Solitaire is said to have been written by a Microsoft intern, Wes Cherry

ch.say: Tap a card to flip it!
cards: Because it takes patience to sort the cards
On Windows, the cards famously bounce off in a cascade
Can every Klondike deal be won?

ch.say: Enjoy a quiet journey of your own!
p: No one hurrying you — just a conversation between you and the cards.
